name: Play 5–10 songs on ukulele
blurb: Four nylon strings, short scale, forgiving action — the ukulele gets you playing real songs faster than any other instrument. Four chords cover an enormous amount of popular music.
steps: Tune it (G-C-E-A) and learn to retune before every session — new strings drift constantly for the first fortnight.
Learn C, F, Am and G. That set alone plays hundreds of songs.
Drill the chord changes without strumming: one minute per pair, counting how many clean changes you make, and beat the number tomorrow.
Learn a basic down-down-up-up-down-up strum and keep it going even while changing chords.
Learn your first full song end to end, including the part where you mess up and carry on.
Add G7, Dm and Em, then build a five-song set you can play without a chart.
tips: Buzzing means your fingers are flat rather than arched, or too far from the fret.
Practise the changes, not the chords. Everyone can hold a C; the skill is arriving at it in time.
Sing while you play as soon as possible, badly. It forces the strumming to become automatic.
proof: You play five songs start to finish, from memory, singing along, without stopping.
